subject: /tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-native-wire-owner-subject-03
verdictSummary: The three review-02 required findings are substantively addressed. I reproduced check.py 373/0 and selftest 78/78 from the 35 declared inputs only. My own tools reproduce the pattern closure (54 sites, 53 lowerings) and the byte arithmetic (67108864, 9663676416, 796198). Four new required findings remain. (1) A Native2 CanonicalPath extern path member can hide a real '..' segment behind a line terminator. Both the owner and the candidate carrier admit it on the wire, and the closed path law covers only one extern member. (2) The declared ECMA dialect and the owner Python re evaluation are not reconciled. For 'a/..\n', a legal dependency file name, the owner set admission and the successor raise an untyped exception, so there is no admission and no route. (3) The published prepared route row says 'explicitly selected', but the executed selector also refuses in defaulted mode, and either behaviour passes every check. (4) Greedy chunking is not bound to the host sender and is not byte-minimal, so the planner's acceptance does not constrain the actual request.

assessments.boundarySizing: Accepted. The owner rust2 limitPolicy.aggregateAccounting states that 'Request/response payload totals include exact canonical-CBOR envelope payload bytes and exclude each 40-byte transport prefix', and framing.lengthScope is 'payload bytes only', so excluding the prefix is owner law, not an author choice. My deterministic-CBOR length function matches the owner provider_wire_model.wire_cbor on 216 materialized chunk frames spanning the sequence, index, offset and byte-string head thresholds. The closed form equals the materialized 3-chunk total (2098121). Independently recomputed: the dependency manifest is 204 bytes per 24-scalar entry, maxUniform24 is 328963, and the published groups give exactly 67108864 and 67108865; the request is exactly 9663676416 and 9663676417 over 9222 frames; the small request is 6834 bytes in 10 frames; the frame bound is 796198 (minimal dependency entry 116 bytes, minimal snapshot entry 135 bytes). No multi-GiB allocation was made; lengths come from real small encodes plus closed form.
assessments.chunkUnitsAndMetadata: Chunk bytes are 1..max per rust2 (PreparedOutputChunk 'non-empty byte string 1..maxPreparedOutputChunkBytes'). A zero-length entry has no chunk (CHUNK-CUSTODY), and the Seal carries totalChunkCount. Greedy chunking minimizes frame count. It is byte-minimal on 10683 exhaustive compositions below the CBOR head thresholds, but not across them: owner-encoded [6,24] = 457 bytes and [7,23] = 456 bytes versus greedy [24,6] = 458. At the real 1 MiB chunk size the gap is a few bytes per file (for example, byteOffset heads crossing 2^32). See RF-4 for the binding consequence.
assessments.cancellationMeaning: Accepted as an author choice with a clear meaning. P3-29 admits exactly one Cancel from *PRE_COMPLETE, and Cancel reason is const 'user-interrupt'. aggregateAccounting counts every host-to-worker envelope, so reserving the exact Cancel (151 bytes, 1 frame at the boundary) keeps a user interrupt representable (D9 interrupted, 130) instead of turning it into a worker limit fault. Cost: a request that fits only without the Cancel (9663676265 + 151) is refused. The contract should state this meaning explicitly (A-7).
assessments.preSpawnClosure: The dependency set (before PlanId), the prepared set (before Plan construction) and the Plan-time planner cover frames, request totals and request frames. Residues are RF-1 to RF-4 and A-3 to A-6.

requiredFindings.title: Planner acceptance does not bind the host sender's chunking, and greedy chunking is not byte-minimal
evidence: REQUEST-WIRE-ACCOUNTING says the host 'plans' the sequence and that 'Chunks are params.chunking'. No rule requires the host to SEND that chunking. CHUNK-CUSTODY and rust2 require only contiguous chunks of 1..max bytes.

A host emitting smaller lawful chunks after planner acceptance can exceed maxRequestPayloadBytesTotal or maxRequestFrames. For example, at the 9663676416 accept vector, any extra chunk frame adds at least 100 payload bytes and one frame. The worker then applies limitPolicy and the run becomes a protocol fault for an input the host accepted.

On the refusal side, greedy is frame-minimal but not byte-minimal. Owner wire_cbor gives [6,24] = 457 and [7,23] = 456 against greedy [24,6] = 458 at c=24 (scratch/probe_accounting.out.json). A greedy refusal at the exact byte boundary therefore does not prove that no lawful chunking fits; at 1 MiB chunks the gap is a few bytes per file.
requiredFindings.fix: Make the planned sequence normative for the host sender: every chunk except an entry's last carries exactly maxChunkBytes, zero-length entries have none, and the host emits exactly the planned frames. State that the refusal is 'under the normative host chunking', not 'no lawful encoding'. Add a control where a non-greedy host transcript for an accepted plan is non-conforming.

That wrote tools/__pycache__/filelist.cpython-314.pyc and common.cpython-314.pyc into the subject; the before-walk had completed earlier in the same script and saw 64 files. The first after-check found 66 files. The mtimes match my scripts, so I removed exactly those two .pyc files and the empty __pycache__ directory. All reproduction ran from scratch/copy with -I -B and forced pycache prefixes, so the stray files were never read by check.py or selftest.py.
